routes.label: Find the angles of triangle CRT

question:
In triangle \(CAT,\) we have \(\angle ACT =\angle ATC\) and \(\angle CAT = 36^\circ.\) If \(\overline{TR}\) bisects \(\angle ATC,\) then \(\angle CRT =\)

[Figure 1](figures/2000_AMC_8_Q13_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
[Figure 1](figures/2000_AMC_8_Q13_question_fig1.svg)

First find the two equal angles in triangle \(CAT\). Since a triangle's angles sum to \(180^\circ\),
\[
\angle ACT=\angle ATC=\frac{180^\circ-36^\circ}{2}=72^\circ.
\]
The angle bisector \(TR\) divides the angle at \(T\) into equal halves, so \(\angle CTR=36^\circ\). The figure places \(R\) on \(AC\), which means \(\angle RCT=\angle ACT=72^\circ\). Now triangle \(CRT\) has two known angles, giving
\[
\angle CRT=180^\circ-72^\circ-36^\circ=72^\circ.
\]
Thus the answer is \(\boxed{72^\circ}\), choice C.
